brewing.notes: A safe starting point for green tea: cooler water, short steeps, then adjust by taste.

description:
Burmese pickled tea from Mogok, made only from young leaves.

Treat it as you would any green tea: cooler water, short steeps, and a seller who can say where and when it was picked.
history: Many eaters prefer it for that reason, over kinds that mix in coarser leaves. Little more is documented about it.
processing: Only young tea leaves are pickled.
harvest_season: Usually picked in spring, with the earliest pickings prized, as with most green teas.
appearance_dry: Green leaf whose shape depends on the maker, as is usual for regional green teas.
appearance_wet: Usually soft green leaf that opens up in the water.
taste_profile: Expect what green teas usually give: fresh, vegetal and lightly sweet.
vintage_note: Green teas like this are normally sold as the current year's harvest and are best within a year of picking. It is not an ageing tea.
